mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the inflation signal, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the labor market signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous 2 months signals increased economic activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the housing starts signal, or if the correlation between HOUST changes and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) over a 2-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous 2 months signals a slowdown in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the industrial production signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO changes and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the combined signal, or if the interaction term between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over the previous month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3 percentage points, the combined signal indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the combined labor signal, or if the interaction term between PAYEMS and UNRATE is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) over a 2-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the previous 3 months signals robust consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances following RSAFS increases, or if the correlation between RSAFS and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) over a 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative, the combination signals an accommodative monetary policy with a contracting economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the combined signal, or if the interaction term between FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) over a 3-year period.
